title: OpenAI donates $5 million to help mathematicians ‘understand’ AI after backlash
source_used: TokenPost (Independent paywalled; Crypto Briefing and NDTV blocked)
key_facts: OpenAI commits $5 million to a Simons Foundation program that funds mathematicians reviewing AI-generated work.
The effort combines $15 million in funding and resources from OpenAI, Anthropic and the Simons Foundation.
It pays for workshops, conferences and special programs; the foundation runs an open call for proposals; OpenAI and Anthropic also supply AI tools and computing.
On 6 Oct OpenAI released 722 manuscripts across 372 result families; three were withdrawn on 7 Oct after a sign error, leaving 719.
Some manuscripts lack Lean formalizations and may contain issues.
Simons Foundation President David Spergel: the goal is to support the mathematics community.
quote_evidence: The overall effort brings together $15 million in combined funding and resources from OpenAI, Anthropic and the Simons Foundation.
Three manuscripts were withdrawn Oct. 7 after a sign error invalidated an argument and a construction used by two related papers.
why_it_matters_hint: Mathematicians face a flood of AI-written results and now get funding to check them.
notes: Independent text paywalled; read TokenPost. Independent's headline frames it as coming after a backlash; TokenPost does not use that framing. Follow-up of our 15 Oct item on OpenAI's 372 math results (Technology Org).
